root_idea.summary: The root has two principal semantic orientations: moving away or becoming exposed and manifest, and intensity, greatness, or severity.
root_idea.development: The first orientation extends from departure to openness, revelation, and related terms for exposed land, winds, and passing omens. A second branch develops toward extraordinary magnitude, hardship, distress, and force.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic forms are imperfect forms of the Form I verb بَرِحَ; the public headword is normalized to the Classical Arabic perfect citation form.

senses.definition: To go away, depart, or quit a place.
senses.usage_conditions: Attributive use. In the Quranic occurrence at 12:80, the verb is negated in لَنْ أَبْرَحَ, giving the sense “I will not leave.”

senses.definition: To cease, stop, or discontinue; in a negative construction, to remain or continue.
senses.usage_conditions: Non-attributive use, often with a predicate or an understood activity. The Quranic لا/لن أبرح constructions express continuing or not ceasing until a stated or understood goal is reached.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become manifest or revealed after being concealed; for a hidden matter or secret, to come into the open.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Often used in the expression بَرِحَ الْخَفَاءُ, literally indicating that concealment has departed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the wind: to carry up, raise, or sweep up and scatter dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical extension in which the wind is understood to go away with the dust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a hunted gazelle, bird, or other wild animal: to pass across the observer’s field of view with its side turned toward him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported direction varies by regional usage; the term is contrasted with سَنَحَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become angry or be intensely angered with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing the intensity of a person’s anger toward another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To affect severely; to afflict, distress, hurt, harass by importunity, or torment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of fever, anxiety, trouble, a painful beating, or a person who presses another with annoying insistence; it may also denote severe punishment or torture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove difficulty, distress, or affliction from someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the supplicatory expression بَرَّحَ اللَّهُ عَنْكَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to go away from, depart from, or quit a place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Causative Form IV use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To please, delight, or excite admiration; to honor, magnify, or judge someone or something excellent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an affair that greatly pleases or astonishes, and of a person or thing regarded as exceptionally noble or excellent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exceed customary bounds, degree, or manner; to be extravagant or excessive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with qualities such as generosity or meanness to indicate an extreme or overstepping degree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Difficulty, distress, affliction, adversity, severe annoyance, or a calamity; also an exceptionally grave or remarkable event.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in phrases for experiencing hardship or calamity, including بِنْتُ بَرْحٍ and related expressions, and in imprecations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The best or finest of something, especially one of the finest camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May be used of a male or female camel and is also extended to the best specimens of a class.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An exclamation uttered when a shooter or caster misses the mark.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression contrasted with مَرْحَى, said when the mark is hit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A severe paroxysm, violent attack, or intense distress, especially of fever; also vehement mental distress associated with oppressive inspiration or revelation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is used for the severe phase of an illness and in a specialized account of overwhelming mental or spiritual distress.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An open, spacious tract of land without buildings, trees, vegetation, or habitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: By extension, any exposed, uncovered, conspicuous place free of things that conceal it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lion; figuratively, a courageous man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic appellation portraying the subject as fixed in place and not departing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Plainly, openly, or manifestly; an affair or matter that is public and evident.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adverbially with expressions such as جَاءَ بِالأَمْرِ بَرَاحًا, “he made the matter plain.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Counsel or an opinion regarded as disapproved or evil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized evaluative use of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for the sun, especially in the expression دَلَكَتْ بَرَاحِ, referring to its setting or decline from the meridian.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is determinate and may be indeclinable in this usage; variant readings of the expression are reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The croaking or cry of a crow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical use associated with the crow’s characteristic cry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The crow, including the raven and related kinds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A determinate appellation; the plural expression is بَنَاتُ بَرِيحٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A saying that confirms that a person has spoken or acted rightly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional phrase used to endorse the correctness of someone’s statement or action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a hunted animal or bird: passing with its side turned across the observer’s line of sight; by extension, an inauspicious or ill-omened sign.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The precise direction differs between regional traditions, and the omen may consequently be regarded as unfavorable or, by some groups, differently interpreted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A manner of twisting that is contrary to the usual or proper manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction derived from the directional sense of بَارِحٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An action that has not been performed rightly or correctly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of an improperly executed act.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hot or violent wind, especially one that raises and scatters dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural بَوَارِحُ may refer to seasonal hot or forceful winds and their dust-bearing effects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disputed usage for the anواʾ, the star-settings associated with seasonal weather.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This attribution is reported as a minority or contested interpretation rather than an undisputed lexical meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The preceding or most recently past night; yesternight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is understood as referring to the night that has gone away; in later usage it may also mean yesterday.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A conventional comparison expressing resemblance between two things, literally likening the present night to the previous one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of any two things that resemble each other, not only of nights.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More difficult, distressing, or afflicting; most severe or intense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used comparatively or intensively of an affair, and in expressions such as “a most severe slaughter.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Difficulties, distresses, afflictions, or adversities; burdensome hardships incurred through troublesome means of subsistence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural noun derived from the Form II branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The burning or fierce pangs of yearning and longing desire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for the intense affliction of longing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Importuned or pressed with annoying insistence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used predicatively of a person subjected to persistent molestation or pressure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Severe, afflicting, distressing, or harassing; of a beating, causing intense pain; of a person, annoying through importunity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial adjective covering severe effects on affairs, events, blows, or people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The root of the wild mandrake or related plant, traditionally described as human-shaped and medicinal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plant name, distinct from the core verbal and abstract branches of the root.

cautions: The public headword is normalized to بَرِحَ, the Form I perfect citation form; QAC’s أَبْرَحَ is an internal lemma identity reflecting the attested imperfect forms.
The Quranic occurrences are all in negative constructions, so translations such as “will I leave” and “will cease” reflect the interaction of lexical meaning with negation and construction.
The directional interpretation of بَارِحٌ varies among regional traditions, and the use of البَوَارِحُ for الأَنْوَاءُ is explicitly disputed.
